NO. 013 · Songbirds & City Birds / Sturnidae · Starlings & Mynas

Red-billed Starling

丝光椋鸟 · sī guāng liáng niǎo Spodiopsar sericeus
Winter visitor Common 22–24 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

White head, grey body, red bill and red legs — a starling of the south

The male's head looks dusted with silk: pale grey-white with a satin sheen, set off by a coral-red bill. The Red-billed Starling is endemic to China; in winter a flock will descend on a fruiting tree and strip it bare.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • MaleHead and neck pale grey-white with a silky sheen; upperparts grey; wings black with white patches; tail black.
  • FemaleOverall grey-brown, the head not pale, plumage plain — easily separated from the male.
  • Bill & legsBill coral red with a darker tip; legs orange-red and bright.
  • Around the eyeBare orange-yellow skin around the eye, often read as an eye-ring, conspicuous against the pale head.

Behaviour

A highly gregarious, tree-loving starling, gathering in winter in flocks of tens to over a hundred to feed on berries, and dropping to the ground for fallen fruit and insects. A winter visitor here from October to March in farmland, orchards and city parks. Roosts communally in street trees or bamboo.

Voice

Noisy: a harsh single 'jriii' or 'chreee', very loud when the whole flock calls, with softer whistles mixed in.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Doumen orchards
  • Jinwan farmland
  • Xiangshan Lake Park
  • Tangjiawan old trees
Field note
Against Crested Myna and Black-collared Starling: the Red-billed Starling is the palest of the three, with a grey-white head and neck and a red bill.
